I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt (386/387 files SHA-256 verified; LICENSE elided, export.sh self-referential) and found the cause of the failure. I then verified it against a real PostgreSQL, so this is observed rather than reasoned.

The failure
TheSchemaRefusesEveryForbiddenShapeOfAnEventRow probes the vocabulary constraint with ('loved', 'Anything'). That row breaks two CHECKs at once — ..._type_vocabulary ('loved' is not in the list) and ..._body_payload ((event_type='submitted') = (body IS NOT NULL) is false = true). PostgreSQL evaluates CHECKs in name order, so body_payload sorts first and is the name reported. The assertion reached past what it could decide.

Confirmed empirically just now:

loved + 'Anything'  -> body_payload        (the failure you saw)
loved + NULL        -> type_vocabulary     (the repair)
The repair (F-123)
Each probe row now breaks exactly one constraint, and that property is itself proven rather than assumed: every probe is paired with a control row differing in one attribute, inserted inside a transaction and rolled back. If a probe were over-determined, its control would be refused too and the fact fails by name. Verified against the real DDL — all five probes name their own constraint, all four controls insert, final row count 0.

The fifth probe (body_within_cap) is added, plus a catalogue assertion that the table's CHECK set is exactly those four — so "every forbidden shape" is now computed rather than claimed. Still 13 [Fact]; §16.4's count does not move.

The container chatter (F-124)
Testcontainers logs every create, readiness probe and delete at Information through its own console logger — several hundred lines that buried the one failing assertion. Both fixtures now set TestcontainersSettings.Logger = NullLogger.Instance as the first statement inside their existing try, where a throw still becomes a skip. What diagnoses a container that won't start here is the fixture's own DescribeFailure prose, which is better than those lines anyway.

Gated by a new ContainerLoggingContractTests — 2 assertions, subjects computed from the tree (files constructing a PostgreSqlBuilder, floor of 2), asserting each installs the logger and installs it before it builds. Both proven sensitive against planted defects.
